heading: Read a hosting metric with its denominator and costs
body:
Occupancy, average nightly rate, gross revenue, and cash flow describe different parts of a rental operation. A useful performance review states the period, available nights, booked nights, cancellations, charges included, and costs excluded. Without those definitions, two apparently similar results may not be comparable.

For a fictional property, 18 booked nights out of 30 available nights produces 60% occupancy. Blocking ten nights for owner use changes the availability denominator. If the report instead shows 18 booked nights out of 20 available nights, the displayed occupancy becomes 90% even though paid nights did not increase. Preserve both the booking count and the reason for unavailable nights.

Similarly, separate accommodation revenue from cleaning charges, taxes collected, platform deductions, refunds, and operating costs. Review the payout reconciliation before treating gross bookings as spendable cash. Keep financing payments and replacement reserves visible in the cash plan.

Use the answer library to investigate the metric behind the headline. The goal of a monthly review is a specific operating decision: improve availability, adjust pricing, investigate costs, or obtain better evidence. A higher percentage is useful only when you understand what changed.
